.github/workflows/ci.yml.predecessor_utf8:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# Concurrency is per-JOB: a newer push to the same PR or branch cancels that
# ref's in-flight `checks` and `e2e`. Both are safe to cancel — `e2e` runs
# against its own throwaway Supabase, so nothing is left dirty.
#
# `checks` and `e2e` run side by side (both start as soon as `changes` says the
# diff touches the app), so a push takes as long as the slower of the two, not
# their sum. Measured on a passing run: checks ~2m20s, e2e ~6m55s; in series
# that was ~9m40s from push to green. The cost is that a lint or type error no
# longer stops e2e before it starts, so a push with one wastes that e2e run.

jobs:
  # Docs-only changes (docs/, pitch/, mockups/, prototypes/, Markdown outside
  # content/) skip the ~10 runner-minute checks + E2E run. The jobs are skipped
  # with `if:`, not filtered with `paths-ignore`, so they still report their
  # check names (as "skipped", which satisfies a required status check) and a
  # docs-only PR can merge. Anything else, or any doubt (a diff that can't be
  # computed), runs everything. content/ always counts: the app imports its
  # JSON and the unit tests read its Markdown.
  changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      app: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.app }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Check this draft's exact head; other branches keep their standard checkout.
          ref: ${{ (github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-151-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-152-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-154-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-156-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-161-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-162-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-163-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-164-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-165-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-171-carole-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-172-carole-handoff') && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - id: diff
        env:
          # pull_request checks out the PR's merge commit, whose first parent
          # is this base SHA, so the diff is exactly what the PR changes.
          BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
        run: |
          set -u
          app=true
          if git fetch --quiet --depth=1 origin "$BASE" 2>/dev/null \
            && changed=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD) && [ -n "$changed" ]; then
            app=false
            while IFS= read -r f; do
              case "$f" in
                content/*) app=true ;;
                docs/*|pitch/*|mockups/*|prototypes/*|.claude/*|.agents/*|*.md) ;;
                *) app=true ;;
              esac
            done <<< "$changed"
            echo "Changed files:"; echo "$changed"
          fi
          echo "app=$app" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # Pure local checks: fully parallel across PRs, fast feedback.
  checks:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: checks-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Check this draft's exact head; other branches keep their standard checkout.
          ref: ${{ (github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-151-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-152-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-154-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-156-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-161-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-162-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-163-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-164-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-165-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-171-carole-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-172-carole-handoff') && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Validate Gabay course source
        run: npm run gabay:check

      - name: Validate Gabay KB source
        run: npm run gabay:kb:check

      - name: Verify approved Gabay release package
        run: npm run gabay:release:check

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm run test

  e2e:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Each run gets its OWN throwaway Supabase, built by `supabase start` from
    # supabase/migrations/ and seeded by supabase/seed.sql (the four stable
    # fixture accounts plus the pilot's resting feature flags). Nothing here
    # touches the pilot project any more: E2E used to write into it on every
    # PR, and the specs, their purges and the flag flips were a large share of
    # the pilot's Disk IO budget on the free plan — see docs/deploy-runbook.md's
    # "E2E database" section.
    #
    # Because nothing is shared, runs can overlap and a cancelled run leaves
    # nothing behind, so this job is cancellable like `checks` and needs no
    # queueing (the old e2e-wait job and e2e-shared-supabase-project group).
    concurrency:
      group: e2e-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    env:
      # The local stack's well-known demo URL, anon key and the seed's fixture
      # password. None of these are secrets: they only ever unlock the
      # throwaway database this job starts and discards.
      NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: http://127.0.0.1:54321
      NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJzdXBhYmFzZS1kZW1vIiwicm9sZSI6ImFub24iLCJleHAiOjE5ODM4MTI5OTZ9.CRXP1A7WOeoJeXxjNni43kdQwgnWNReilDMblYTn_I0
      E2E_STABLE_BHW_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password
      E2E_STABLE_ADMIN_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password
      E2E_OTHER_BARANGAY_BHW_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password
      E2E_STABLE_CITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password
      E2E_STABLE_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password
      # The seed turns ai_external + ai_gap_draft on, as on the pilot, so
      # e2e/ai-gap-draft.spec.ts runs its real round trip and needs a provider
      # key; each run spends a small amount of Gemini quota. GEMINI_MODEL is
      # optional.
      GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
      GEMINI_MODEL: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_MODEL }}
      SENTRY_DSN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_DSN }}
      NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_DSN }}
      SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
      SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
      SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Check this draft's exact head; other branches keep their standard checkout.
          ref: ${{ (github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-151-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-152-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-154-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-156-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-161-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-162-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-163-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-164-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-165-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-171-carole-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-172-carole-handoff') && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1
        with:
          version: 2.118.0

      # Chromium for Playwright. A cache hit skips the ~150 MB download; the
      # install command below still runs to add the system packages.
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('package-lock.json') }}

      # The three slowest setup steps need nothing from each other, so they run
      # together instead of one after another (~65s Supabase start, ~41s build,
      # ~26s browser install, ~2m10s in series). The build does not need the
      # database: no route is statically generated. Only what the app and specs
      # call is started: Postgres, Auth, PostgREST, Storage and the Kong
      # gateway in front of them. Background output is held in log files and
      # printed in groups after, so it stays readable and a failure shows its log.
      - name: Start local Supabase, build the app and install browsers (in parallel)
        run: |
          npm run build > build.log 2>&1 &
          build_pid=$!
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium > playwright.log 2>&1 &
          playwright_pid=$!

          status=0
          supabase start -x realtime,imgproxy,mailpit,postgres-meta,studio,edge-runtime,logflare,vector,supavisor || status=1
          wait "$build_pid" || { echo "::error::build failed"; status=1; }
          wait "$playwright_pid" || { echo "::error::playwright install failed"; status=1; }

          echo "::group::npm run build"; cat build.log; echo "::endgroup::"
          echo "::group::playwright install"; cat playwright.log; echo "::endgroup::"
          exit "$status"

      # The HHP-NCD corpus the Chat Guide specs answer from, loaded and
      # published through the admin RPCs exactly as it was on the pilot.
      - name: Load KB content into local Supabase
        run: npm run kb:load -- --project local --apply --publish --owner admin.stable
        env:
          KB_LOADER_USERNAME: admin.stable
          KB_LOADER_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password

      # P4 content is published only in this job's disposable database, so
      # browser tests can verify the Chat Guide end to end. The loader rejects
      # every nonlocal target for this corpus.
      - name: Load Gabay KB into disposable Supabase
        run: npm run kb:load -- --project local --corpus philhealth-gabay --apply --publish --owner admin.stable
        env:
          KB_LOADER_USERNAME: admin.stable
          KB_LOADER_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password

      - name: Load Gabay course as a local draft
        run: npm run gabay:load -- --apply --project local --org-unit "Batong Malake" --owner admin.stable
        env:
          KB_LOADER_USERNAME: admin.stable
          KB_LOADER_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password

      - name: Rehearse Gabay course publication in disposable Supabase
        run: npm run gabay:publish -- --apply --project local --org-unit "Batong Malake" --owner admin.stable
        env:
          KB_LOADER_USERNAME: admin.stable
          KB_LOADER_PASSWORD: local-e2e-password

      - name: E2E smoke tests
        run: npm run e2e
        env:
          CI: true
          # The suite runs serially as a few shared test users, so specs that
          # each send chat requests starve one another at the default 20/min.
          # chat-guide.spec.ts reads this to size its 429 flood.
          CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE: 60

      - name: Upload Playwright traces
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-test-results
          path: test-results/
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # ~70s, so it runs on pushes to main (after merge) rather than on every
      # PR push: a performance-budget regression is caught right after it merges
      # instead of before. Re-enable it for PRs by dropping this condition.
      - name: Performance budget check (Lighthouse)
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: npx lhci autorun --config=lighthouserc.js

.github/workflows/remotion.yml.predecessor_utf8:
name: Remotion clips

# INC-28 tier 2 (docs/training-modules-plan.md). Proves every committed
# composition in remotion/ still lints, typechecks and renders to the lesson
# format (480p H.264 + last-frame poster) within the size budget, and keeps
# the render as a downloadable artifact for review. It does NOT replace the
# committed files under public/training/: renders are not byte-reproducible
# across machines, so a lesson's hashed clip is re-rendered locally with
# `npm run remotion:render -- <id> <name> --public <dir>` and committed with
# its new lesson.json hashes, like every other training asset.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "remotion/**"
      - "scripts/remotion-render.mjs"
      - "scripts/lesson-161-*.mjs"
      - "scripts/lesson-162-*"
      - "docs/lesson-162-*"
      - "scripts/lesson-163-*.mjs"
      - ".github/workflows/lesson163-media.yml"
      - ".github/workflows/remotion.yml"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "remotion/**"
      - "scripts/remotion-render.mjs"
      - "scripts/lesson-161-*.mjs"
      - "scripts/lesson-162-*"
      - "docs/lesson-162-*"
      - "scripts/lesson-163-*.mjs"
      - ".github/workflows/lesson163-media.yml"
      - ".github/workflows/remotion.yml"

concurrency:
  group: remotion-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  render:
    # Split the complete library across eight runners. The 88-composition
    # regression reached nearly 30 minutes on four; retain every check and clip.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Preserve every clip, poster, size-budget check and downloadable artifact.
    # Eight shards leave room for rendering and uploading every composition.
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Check this draft's exact head; other branches keep their standard checkout.
          ref: ${{ (github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-151-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-152-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-154-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-156-malou-proposal' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-161-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-162-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-163-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-164-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-165-enhancement-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-171-carole-handoff' || github.head_ref == 'codex/lesson-172-carole-handoff') && github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: remotion/package-lock.json

      - name: Install Remotion project
        working-directory: remotion
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint and typecheck
        working-directory: remotion
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Install Remotion's headless browser
        working-directory: remotion
        run: npx remotion browser ensure

      - name: Render every composition
        env:
          RENDER_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # `--quiet` ends with the IDs space-separated on one line; split
          # that line and keep only ID-shaped words.
          ids=$(cd remotion && npx remotion compositions --quiet | tail -n 1 | tr -s ' \t' '\n' | grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$')
          index=0
          for id in $ids; do
            if [ "$((index % 8))" -eq "$RENDER_SHARD" ]; then
              node scripts/remotion-render.mjs "$id" 2>&1 | tee -a render.log
            fi
            index=$((index + 1))
          done
          if grep -q "warn .* exceeds" render.log; then
            echo "::error::A clip exceeds the INC-28 size budget (see log above)"
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: remotion-renders-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: remotion/out/
          retention-days: 14

content/training/day1-basic-competencies.predecessor_utf8:
## [purpose] Purpose

In a sample health-station and field-visit setting, identify five hazard groups and match one observed hazard to potential harm, immediate control and reporting contact.

## [time-materials] Time and materials

45 minutes of facilitated practice within the subchapter's 4 hours; short Read completion does not replace that training. Use the scenario and checklist below, paper and a pen. No real personal records in practice.

## [prepare] Prepare

Use a paper scenario, not a hazardous work area. Prepare the local reporting contact.

## [opening] Opening

The entrance floor is wet. Which report supports immediate action?

## [steps] Steps

Read the situation. Model one attempt against the Observe checklist. Run the practice in pairs or triads. Give specific feedback and repeat the part needing improvement. Ask the check before revealing the explanation.

## [expected-answers] Expected answers

The first report gives location, risk and action. A reminder alone does not remove the hazard; absence of injury now is no reason to wait.

## [misconception] Common misconception

Misses the hazard or gives only “be careful” as the response. Recognizing a hazard should lead to a specific control and responsible contact.

## [practice] Practice activity

Draw five boxes: needlestick injury; infection exposure; body discomfort; stress from excessive work; work-related accidents. Give a station or home-visit example for each. Choose one and write the harm, control and contact. In pairs, replace a vague “be careful” with a specific action. Alone, use the checklist. Before the next duty, perform a short hazard check.

## [answer-key] Answer key

1. “Wet entrance, slip risk; keep people away and arrange correction with responsible staff.”

The first report gives location, risk and action. A reminder alone does not remove the hazard; absence of injury now is no reason to wait.

## [observe] Observe

Identifies all five hazard groups and gives potential harm, immediate control and a reporting contact for the chosen example.

Ready: Identifies all five hazard groups and gives potential harm, immediate control and a reporting contact for the chosen example. Completes this without prompting.

Needs practice: Names the hazard but omits contact or control; complete all four fields and repeat.

Not yet: Misses the hazard or gives only “be careful” as the response.

Mark each criterion done / prompted / not yet and record the exact words or action. Peer feedback is practice; staff observations cover only performances actually observed. One demonstration does not establish that everyone is ready.

## [support] Support

Names the hazard but omits contact or control; complete all four fields and repeat. Allow spoken or written responses and reading assistance. Use the participant’s preferred language while keeping the same criteria.

## [sources-review] Sources and review notes

Draft for review. DOH Facilitator Guide: PDF 30; BHW Reference Manual: PDF 21, 22, 23. The five hazard groups span both source-table pages. A local clinical trainer must review demonstrations and referral pathways. Immediate needlestick evaluation was checked against CDC on 25 September 2026. Outstanding visual, audio, source and pilot checks are in the separate review report. No new certification rule.

## [purpose] Layunin

Sa halimbawang health station at field visit, tukuyin ang limang uri ng panganib at ipares ang isang nakitang panganib sa posibleng pinsala, agarang kontrol at reporting contact.

## [time-materials] Oras at kagamitan

45 minuto para sa pinadali na pagsasanay. Bahagi ito ng 4 oras ng subchapter; ang maikling Read ay hindi kapalit ng buong pagsasanay. Gamitin ang sitwasyon at checklist sa ibaba, papel at panulat. Walang tunay na personal na rekord sa pagsasanay.

## [prepare] Ihanda

Gamitin ang scenario sa papel, hindi tunay na mapanganib na lugar. Ihanda ang lokal na reporting contact.

## [opening] Pambungad

May basang sahig sa pasukan. Aling ulat ang magagamit agad?

## [steps] Mga hakbang

Basahin ang sitwasyon. Ipakita ang isang halimbawa gamit ang checklist sa Obserbahan. Ipagawa ang pagsasanay sa pares o tatluhan. Magbigay ng tiyak na feedback at ipaulit ang bahaging kailangan pang ayusin. Ibigay ang check bago ipakita ang paliwanag.

## [expected-answers] Inaasahang sagot

Ang unang ulat ay may lugar, panganib at aksyon. Ang paalala lamang ay hindi nag-aalis ng panganib; ang kawalan ng pinsala ngayon ay hindi dahilan para maghintay.

## [misconception] Karaniwang pagkakamali

Hindi nakikita ang panganib o paalalang “mag-ingat” lang ang aksyon. Ang pagkilala sa panganib ay dapat humantong sa tiyak na kontrol at taong tutugon.

## [practice] Gawaing pagsasanay

Iguhit ang limang kahon: tusok ng karayom; exposure sa impeksyon; pananakit ng katawan; stress sa sobrang trabaho; aksidente sa gawain. Magbigay ng isang halimbawa sa bawat isa mula sa station o home visit. Pumili ng isa at isulat ang pinsala, kontrol at contact. Sa pares, suriin kung “mag-ingat” lang ang kontrol at palitan ng tiyak na aksyon. Kung mag-isa, gamitin ang checklist. Bago ang susunod na duty, magsagawa ng maikling hazard check.

## [answer-key] Susi sa sagot

1. “Basang pasukan, panganib madulas; ilayo muna ang tao at ipatama sa responsableng staff.”

Ang unang ulat ay may lugar, panganib at aksyon. Ang paalala lamang ay hindi nag-aalis ng panganib; ang kawalan ng pinsala ngayon ay hindi dahilan para maghintay.

## [observe] Obserbahan

Natutukoy ang limang hazard group; sa napiling halimbawa, may posibleng pinsala, agarang kontrol at taong lalapitan.

Kaya na: Natutukoy ang limang hazard group; sa napiling halimbawa, may posibleng pinsala, agarang kontrol at taong lalapitan. Nagagawa kahit hindi pinapaalalahanan.

Kailangan pang magsanay: Natutukoy ang panganib ngunit kulang ang contact o kontrol; ipapunan ang apat na field bago ulitin.

Hindi pa: Hindi nakikita ang panganib o paalalang “mag-ingat” lang ang aksyon.

Markahan bawat pamantayan ng nagawa / may tulong / hindi pa. Magtala ng eksaktong sinabi o ginawa. Ang feedback ng kapareha ay pagsasanay lamang; ang staff observation ay para lamang sa aktuwal na naobserbahan. Huwag markahang lahat ay kaya na dahil may isang nagpakita.

## [support] Tulong

Natutukoy ang panganib ngunit kulang ang contact o kontrol; ipapunan ang apat na field bago ulitin. Maaaring magsalita, magsulat o magpatulong magbasa. Gumamit ng wikang komportable ang kalahok. Panatilihin ang parehong pamantayan.

## [sources-review] Sanggunian at tala sa pagsusuri

Draft para sa pagsusuri. DOH Facilitator Guide: PDF 30; BHW Reference Manual: PDF 21, 22, 23. Ang limang hazard group ay mula sa dalawang pahina ng source table. Suriin ng lokal na clinical trainer ang demo at referral pathway. Ang agarang needlestick evaluation ay sinuri sa CDC noong 25 Setyembre 2026. Nasa hiwalay na review report ang natitirang visual, audio, source at pilot checks. Walang bagong tuntunin sa sertipikasyon.

## [ana] Before Ana starts work

Ana, 33, will assist at the health station before household visits. The entrance floor is wet, the sharps box is nearly full and a hot walk lies ahead. “I will be careful” is not enough. She identifies each hazard, who might be harmed and the control needed. She checks the local protocol and confirms the reporting contact and tasks within her training with the midwife.

## [inspect] Inspect a work area

A fictional station has a wet floor, a blocked exit and no soap at the sink. For each, name the hazard, possible harm, immediate control and reporting contact. First keep people away from danger and seek the right assistance. A checklist that only says “be careful” is incomplete. Check that the problem is corrected before removing the warning.

## [practice] Try it, then repeat

Draw five boxes: needlestick injury; infection exposure; body discomfort; stress from excessive work; work-related accidents. Give a station or home-visit example for each. Choose one and write the harm, control and contact. In pairs, replace a vague “be careful” with a specific action. Alone, use the checklist. Before the next duty, perform a short hazard check.

## [check] Choose the next step

Choose an answer and explain why before viewing the feedback. Then compare it with your own practice attempt.

## [ana] Bago simulan ni Ana ang araw

Si Ana, 33 anyos, ay BHW na tutulong sa health station bago mag-household visit. May basang sahig sa pasukan, halos puno ang sharps box at mainit ang nakaabang na lakad. Hindi sapat ang “mag-iingat ako.” Tinutukoy niya ang hazard, sino ang maaaring masaktan, at anong kontrol ang kailangan. Tinitingnan niya ang lokal na protocol at kinukumpirma sa midwife kung kanino mag-uulat at alin lang ang gawaing saklaw ng kanyang pagsasanay.

## [inspect] Suriin ang isang work area

Sa kathang-isip na station, may basang sahig, nakaharang na labasan at walang sabon sa hugasan. Para sa bawat isa, sabihin ang hazard, maaaring epekto, agarang kontrol at taong aabisuhan. Unahin ang paglayo ng tao sa panganib at paghingi ng tamang tulong. Hindi kumpleto ang checklist kung ang nakasulat ay “mag-ingat” lamang. Balikan kung naayos ang problema bago alisin ang babala.

## [practice] Subukan, saka ulitin

Iguhit ang limang kahon: tusok ng karayom; exposure sa impeksyon; pananakit ng katawan; stress sa sobrang trabaho; aksidente sa gawain. Magbigay ng isang halimbawa sa bawat isa mula sa station o home visit. Pumili ng isa at isulat ang pinsala, kontrol at contact. Sa pares, suriin kung “mag-ingat” lang ang kontrol at palitan ng tiyak na aksyon. Kung mag-isa, gamitin ang checklist. Bago ang susunod na duty, magsagawa ng maikling hazard check.

## [check] Piliin ang susunod na hakbang

Piliin ang sagot at ipaliwanag kung bakit bago tingnan ang feedback. Pagkatapos, ihambing sa sarili mong ginawa sa pagsasanay.
